rows.col_1: GET https://developer.api.autodesk.com/construction/submittals/v2/projects/:projectId/users/me
User context required
data:read
JSON

Must be Bearer <token>, where <token> is a three-legged access token obtained via an Authorization Code flow or a Secure Service Account (SSA) flow.
The SSA flow is designed for headless server-to-server operations. While it functions like a two-legged flow (no user interaction), it is classified as three-legged because it preserves user context.

The ID of the project.
Use the Data Management API to retrieve the project ID. For more information, see the Retrieve a Project ID tutorial. You need to convert the project ID into a project ID for the Forma API by removing the “b." prefix. For example, a project ID of b.a4be0c34a-4ab7 translates to a project ID of a4be0c34a-4ab7.
Returns user details.
Invalid or missing authorization header. Verify the Bearer token and try again.
The user is not authorized to perform this action.
The specified resource was not found.
An unexpected error occurred on the server while processing the request.
The AutodeskId for the current user.
The roles assigned to the user in Submittals. Possible values: 1 - Manager, 2 - User, 4 - Admin
A list of actions that the user is allowed to perform
ID of the action in the format type_of_object::action. For example, item::create, Spec::create.

A mapping of field names to lists of possible values for each field, specific to the associated action. An empty array indicates that there is no specific set of values for those fields.
For example, in the action Spec::create, fields might contain mapping for title (title) and identifier (identifier).

A subset of fields (fields) that are required to perform specific actions, such as creating or transitioning a submittal item. The required fields depend on the user’s role and the action.
For example, creating a submittal item in the mgr-1 state as a manager or in the sbc-1 state as a subcontractor requires different fields. For example, [stateId, specId, title, typeId, manager, managerType].
list of possible transitions
The ID of the transition in the format from-state::to-state. Possible values: create::mgr-1, create::sbc-1.
The descriptive name of the transition. Possible values: Create, Send to Manager, Send to void.
The starting state of the transition.
The unique ID of the starting state. Possible values: create, mgr-1, sbc-1. A rev (review), refers to the state where a submittal item is undergoing revisions or is being reviewed.
The name of the starting state. Possible values: Create, Manager Review, Review.
The target state of the transition.
The unique ID of the target state. For example, mgr-1, mgr-2, void.
The name of the target state. For example, Manager Review, Manager Final Review, Void.
Fields that are used in the transition. For example, [subcontractor, subcontractorType, watchers, responseId].
A list of required fields for the transition. For example, [responseId].
Not relevant
